rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is the M6 opener, delivered before the exercise (maintainer block: 'Lands before the exercise'); body contains no 'the X you did/saw' construction pointing at a completed student beat, so the rule has nothing to check against.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict-before-reveal construction anywhere in the file.
Every chunk carries a self-standing claim (thesis stats, a named story, the generalisation, the compounding move, the framing for what's next); none is a bare wait-state bullet.

Each header matches its chunk's content: 'The numbers' → stats block; 'Things that went sideways' → seven failure stories; 'The generalisation' → the abstracted lesson; 'Then I compounded the session' → the rule-into-skill move; 'What the loop is for' → the framing handoff to the student.

Checked each sub-item per chunk: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere (only single-negation forms, e.g. chunk 0 'Not the pedagogy of it. The actual session.'). Two candidate triples reviewed for weak-third-leg — chunk 5 'The loop exists because LLMs drift... rules leak... every session surprises you, even when the task looked the same' and chunk 3 'The loop caught what the subagents missed. I caught what the loop missed. You will catch what I missed.' — both carry a genuinely new, escalating third leg (a distinct control-for-repetition point; a shift from loop→author→reader) rather than restating legs 1-2, so neither trips the cap. No self-grading superlatives, no number-with-retraction, no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terms like 'the rules file, the tone brief, the session-timing plan' (chunk 3, line 41) read as plain shop language, not repo dialect — `curriculum/evals/ae101-full-reeval-2026-07-12.md:142` confirms this exact phrasing was the deliberately chosen fix for a prior dialect flag ('what an engineer in the room would say'). No 'compendium', 'forcing function', 'beat', 'surface'-as-noun, 'firing', or 'mood' usage in body; 'reference artefact', 'verifier loop', 'plan.md' are arc-earned M5 spine vocabulary, legitimate for this AE101 engineer audience.
